# Per-font fidelity tracker (FF-40)

As of 2026-09-29. Machine-readable source: [font-tracker.json](font-tracker.json). Authored inputs: [font-tracker.overrides.json](font-tracker.overrides.json). Program tracker: [burndown.md](burndown.md) (FF-40 to FF-46). Policy table: [font-licensing.md](font-licensing.md).

This is the per-font work list behind the owner's 2026-09-29 review. Each record holds the family's selected name, preview route and tier, the bundled face (package, version, hashes, styles), the styles it needs and lacks, scripts, per-style measurements, host and native verification, parity signals, phase, status, next action and evidence. Nothing here is a claim of per-family acceptance: every family still needs its own fixture and acceptance record.

160 records: 153 policy families plus 7 shipped script-font dependencies that the policy lacks. 124 route to a face that opf-render bundles; 36 do not. 70 records were read by the committed parity run in a way that is stale against main (rerun needed).

## The owner's plan

Owner input, 2026-09-29, adopted as the program order. Request: "work this in as a tracker and to help prioritize work."

> The owner completed 160 font-specific reviews: all 153 policy registry families plus seven shipped script-font dependencies missing from the registry. No repository files were changed by those reviews.
>
> 1. Reconcile the inventory and establish a fresh baseline. Record each font's selected name, preview face, version, hashes, available styles, scripts, and acceptance evidence.
> 2. Finish loading and style coverage. Connect the shipped editor, gallery, browser, and Node hosts to the intended faces; eliminate unintended fallbacks.
> 3. Prioritize Aptos and Aptos Display compatibility. Measure them separately and qualify candidates before adopting them.
> 4. Complete the remaining replacement work. Packaging, script shaping, and metric compatibility remain separate deliverables.
> 5. Complete native verification and rerun the full parity audit. Keep source, installed-package, and live-site claims separate.
>
> Aptos and Aptos Display are the critical path: each appears in 704 of the 850 audited gallery values.

Rules:

- Every family gets its own fixture and acceptance record. Grouped rows share work, but a result for one family does not establish acceptance for another.
- For proprietary fonts, PPTX always retains the user's selected name.
- Preview replacements must use pinned, permitted files.
- Metric qualification requires per-style measurements, matching line breaks and line metrics, and the unchanged geometry tolerances, not just a favorable average width.
- The current Latin-only corpus must also be extended with script-specific text.
- Most script packs currently provide regular and bold only. Required italic or other styles need genuine qualified faces; diagnostics preserve honesty but do not complete an outstanding fidelity requirement.

## Reconciled with current state

The owner's review predates some merged and in-flight work. The records above use current truth: core `origin/main` policy and docs, the pinned opf-render manifest, and the latest committed parity run. What changed against the review:

- Aptos family (owner review predates this). Intos, Intos Display, Intos Narrow and Intos Serif measured 0.000% mean and maximum width delta in all four styles against Aptos 2.01, with identical vertical metrics and original (Inter-derived; serif Gelasio-derived) outlines under OFL-1.1 with no Reserved Font Name. Independently re-verified for Aptos, Aptos Display and Aptos Narrow; Aptos Serif was measured from Microsoft's Aptos Fonts download. They land in opf#166, opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, none merged yet. Until they merge, main still routes Aptos to Roboto and Aptos Display and Narrow to Carlito, so the tracker records those routes and marks the four families candidate-qualified-landing (the owner's "no verified compatible replacement" is superseded).
- Root-reported parity movement, not committed evidence and not used for priorities: mains 25 perfect, 667 near, 158 mismatch; with the Intos pull requests roughly 640 perfect, 32 near, 178 mismatch. The committed run is 5 perfect, 627 near, 218 mismatch (2026-09-29, table drawn extent). Rerun the audit before using either.
- Georgia now has a metric tier: Gelasio with liga and clig disabled (opf#163, opf-render#49, including the raster ZWNJ fix). The committed parity run predates it and still reports Georgia as a visual substitute.
- Open families are now vendored from unmodified upstream or npm packages (opf-render#50): Open Sans, Montserrat (including 900), Poppins, Bebas Neue, PT Serif, Lora, Merriweather Sans, Source Sans 3 (with the Source Sans Pro alias), Red Hat Display (300, 400, 700) and Red Hat Text (400, 700). Raleway and Playfair Display are not bundled because resvg ignores the wght axis. The owner's "bundle" rows for the bundled families become verification work; the remaining bundling work is Anton, Archivo Narrow, Barlow, Bitter, EB Garamond, Figtree, Libre Caslon Text, Work Sans, Liberation Mono, Sans and Serif, Playfair Display and Raleway.
- Carlito is vendored as unmodified google/fonts files (opf-render#58) because its Reserved Font Name applies. Licenses, Reserved Font Names and no-hotlink rules are guarded in core and the renderer (opf#165, opf-render#53).
- Script fonts: previews now load script faces automatically (opf-render#55, opf-editor#40) and fall back per character to Noto Sans (opf-render#57). The parity run records 109 family uses as `missing` because it models a host without the script pack; those readings are stale until the audit is rerun, and loading is not verification per family.
- The shipped browser hosts still load only the 33 eager faces (base and office packs). The vendored open pack reaches the editor and gallery only with opf-render#54 and opf-editor#42, so families served by that pack carry a loading gap until then.
- Gallery previews use the bundled replacement faces (pptx-gallery#53, #54) and replacement data is published (pptx-gallery#51). This covers gallery cards, not per-family editor verification.
- fontResolution treats a policy look-alike as near, not fail, when the PPTX names the selected family (opf#159). Parity harness fixes merged in opf#164 and opf#168. The value set is 850 after pptx-gallery#40 removed 50 unsupported chart types; Aptos and Aptos Display each appear in 704 of them.
- Selawik 1.01 was measured and rejected as a Segoe UI replacement (opf#166); Red Hat Display stays the visual route. Segoe UI Light, Semilight and Semibold were measured separately.
- Cover slide centering (opf-pptx#97) is geometry work with no font impact.
- The seven shipped script-font dependencies missing from the registry (Noto Sans Arabic, Sinhala, Lao, Myanmar, Thaana, Syriac and Noto Serif Tibetan) are tracked as policy-gap records. Adding their policy rows is follow-up work: this change does not edit font-policy.json.

Inputs: policy version 1 (153 families); opf-render manifest at `eb8c67e7dad84765f8606a4a5c675427af24248f` (49 packages, 131 faces, captured 2026-09-29); measurement report corpus 300 Latin strings; parity run 2026-09-29T19:37:51.028Z at opf `b1fdfa7`, opf-render `762dbb9`, opf-pptx `874d9e9`, pptx-gallery `5963702`.

## Records by phase and class

Columns: Route is the preview face and tier (main's policy; an in-flight route is noted). Bundled lists the styles opf-render ships for the route face and what it lacks. Width delta is mean and maximum |ratio - 1| of shaped advances against the real font on a Latin corpus (per-style values are in the JSON); script families have no script-specific corpus yet. Values counts parity values that use the family.

### Phase 5: Native verification and parity (0)

No family has this as its earliest unfinished phase. Native verification and the full parity rerun (phase 5) apply to every record and are tracked in FF-46 and FF-38.

## Method

- **Selected name.** The PPTX always retains the selected family. The parity typefaces and fontResolution checks read the exported names back for the audited values; the record's `paritySignals.pptxNamedValues` counts them.
- **Route and tier.** From `spec/reference/font-policy.json`, resolving provisional decisions. `metric` needs a mean below 0.1% and a maximum of at most 0.3% in all four styles; `visual` is a documented look-alike. Width deltas alone do not qualify a face: matching line breaks and line metrics, vertical metrics and unchanged geometry tolerances are also required and are unrecorded (`verticalMetricsMatch`, `lineBreaksMatch` are null) except for the in-flight Intos candidate.
- **Bundled.** From the pinned opf-render manifest snapshot: package, version or commit, license, Reserved Font Names, file names and SHA-256 per face. For a proprietary family it describes the route face, never the proprietary font.
- **Styles.** Style keys are weight plus `i` for italic (`400`, `700i`). Required styles come from the measurement report where the real font was on the measuring host, otherwise four styles for Latin and regular and bold for script families are assumed (`stylesBasis`). An open replacement must also carry the styles of every family routed to it (`stylesRequiredByRole`).
- **Parity signals.** From the committed run named above, which models a host without the script pack. `statusAtRun` is what the run observed; `expectedStatusOnMain` is what current main should produce; `rerunNeeded` marks a mismatch.
- **Evidence.** Merged and in-flight pull requests, evidence folders and docs. In-flight work is labelled and never counted as merged.
